text: If/Else branches a flow's path exactly once. Plenty of real processes need something more — they need to repeat the very same set of actions multiple times, once for every item in a list. Flow Designer's native For Each construct does exactly that, and like If/Else, it needs no scripting at all.

A For Each always needs something to iterate over, and that something is itself a data pill — typically the output of an earlier step that returned multiple records instead of just one. A Look Up Records action configured to return every Requested Item associated with a Request produces exactly that kind of multi-record list output.

Everything placed inside a For Each's loop body runs once per item. On every single pass, Flow Designer exposes a brand new pill representing the current item in that iteration, so an action inside the loop can reference that specific item's price or description, exactly the way it would reference a trigger's data pill.

Picture a flow triggered when a Request moves into an approved state. A Look Up Records step returns every Requested Item tied to that Request. Inside the For Each, a single Create Record action builds one fulfillment task per Requested Item — five approved items means the flow ends up creating five separate tasks, automatically.

For Each and If/Else aren't mutually exclusive — an If/Else can live right inside a For Each's loop body, branching differently for every single item on every pass. A loop over Requested Items might check each item's cost against a threshold: cheap items get a fulfillment task immediately, expensive items get routed to extra approval first.
One list, one loop body, one pass per item, re-evaluated fresh every single time. Next up: a worked lab that combines both If/Else and For Each together inside one real flow.
